Traupman 149

sōlus, sōla, sōlum

adjective; gen. sōlīus, dat. sōlī, declension

alone, by oneself

It agrees with the person: sōlus cēnō, I dine alone. Two together with no one else are sōlī (Aug. Conf. 9.10.23). For “the only one”, see only (the only one).

Other words

  • sōlitārius, sōlitāria, sōlitārium — solitary, alone by nature or habit

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 88: sīc nātūra sōlitārium nihil amat; Traupman 155

    Lewis & Short: alone, by itself, lonely.

  • sōlitūdō, sōlitūdinis f. — loneliness, solitude

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.139 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 155

Examples

  • sōlus cēnō, Fabulle, nōn libenter

    I don’t like dining alone, FabullusMart. 11.35.4

  • dīc mihi, quis furor est? … sōlus bōlētōs, Caeciliāne, vorās

    tell me, what madness is this? … you gobble the mushrooms all by yourself, CaecilianusMart. 1.20.1–2

  • sōlus id nōn fēcissem

    on my own I would never have done itAug. Conf. 2.8.16

  • numquam sē minus ōtiōsum esse quam cum ōtiōsus, nec minus sōlum quam cum sōlus esset

    (he used to say) that he was never less idle than when at leisure, nor less alone than when he was aloneCic. Off. 3.1

  • dōnec eris sōspes, multōs numerābis amīcōs: tempora sī fuerint nūbila, sōlus eris

    as long as you prosper you will count many friends; if the skies cloud over, you will be aloneOv. Tr. 1.9.5–6

  • conloquēbāmur ergō sōlī valdē dulciter

    so we talked together, alone, very sweetlyAug. Conf. 9.10.23

See also only, only.
